newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI mulling W.Australia petrochemical plant.
newsitem.headline: ICI mulling W.Australia petrochemical plant.

text.p: Chemicals and plastics group ICI Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it was still reviewing a plan to participate in a consortium to build a petrochemical plant in Western Australia.
"We are still keeping that under review, at this stage it is still not clear whether the ethane is available," managing director Warren Haynes told reporters at a press conference.
"I am not too sure whether there will be a project there, let alone whether or not we are going to be involved," he said.
ICI has previously said it would be a minor player in the project, which has been reported to cost up to A$2.4 billion.
"It is moving along slowly and I think it is a project possibly for the year 2002, taking it from today it is almost impossible for it to be much earlier," Haynes said.
ICI Australia, which is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc, reported a net profit of A$110.7 million for the six months to March 31, compared with A$92.6 million a year earlier.
